name: Belatucadros
text: Belatucadros carries the meaning of fair and shining as a name. He was a god honoured across the northern region of Britain under Roman rule. His devotees gathered most thickly in what people today call Cumberland and Westmorland. Humble soldiers and civilians who were not Roman citizens seem to be the ones who courted his favour. The many ways his name was written suggest his worshippers had little reading skill. In what he stood for he is close to the god Belenus. The Romans linked him with Mars, their deity of war. Some hold that Cocidius is only another form of the same god under Belatucadros. His altars look much like those raised for Vitiris. A few thinkers count him as a forerunner of Bran the Blessed, who is also named Bendigeidfran. Belatucadros appears nowhere with a female partner.

okr.objective: Describe Belatucadros as a war god venerated by common soldiers in northern Britain.
key_results: His name means fair and shining.
He was honoured across northern Britain under Roman rule.
His worshippers came mostly from low-ranking soldiers and non-Roman civilians.
The Romans equated him with the war god Mars.
Some connect his name with the gods Belenus, Cocidius and Vitiris.
He never appears with a consort.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
